description: The kernel's equilibrium, stated in ONE place: the bonds commit pulls, the payoffs the two parties compare, the outcome table, the deterrent gap, and the hypotheses every comparison carries. The asymmetric-bonding paper (/papers/asymmetric-bonding) OWNS the theorem and its proof; docs/THEORY.md binds these figures to the kernel's transfers; formal/lean/FigaroEquilibrium.lean proves the inequalities over the same table; every page that shows a number or a formula from this table renders it from here. scripts/lint-equilibrium-owner.sh fails the commit when any of those surfaces disagrees with this file.

symbols.G: the cumulative value through the order: every payment the process has accumulated so far, this order's own included (G_i = sum of P_j for j <= i)
symbols.r: what the seller can actually retain off-chain by holding out; at most G

hypotheses.dead_process_strictness: r > 0 — on a process that will not close, holding out is strictly better than performing only when the seller retains something; at r = 0 the two are equal

payoffs.basis: the seller's pair is net of what it retains; the buyer's pair is stated on two bases that differ by the constant +P (the delivery the buyer holds), so the inequality is the same on either

a.conditioning: none — the seller's conduct is fixed at that node

b.conditioning: (a), and the buyer's plan: resolve once performance has occurred and not before

theorem.structure: (b) and (c) are the two parties' best-response checks against one profile, jointly a fixed point; (a) is the one unconditional anchor

e.profile: the seller never performs and the buyer resolves regardless
e.status: a second equilibrium, sustained only by a buyer that has given up the instrument the mechanism reserves to it

outcomes_plain.honor: your bond back, and the seller is paid
outcomes_plain.walk_away: your whole bond locked for good, and nobody else gets it
outcomes_plain.seller_forfeits_on_holdout: twice the value at its link, against whatever it kept
